author: Inside Edition
description: A Florida judge is under fire for a courtroom conversation she had with a domestic violence suspect. Christopher Johnson, who appeared before Judge Allison Gilman, is a professional chef. During Johnson’s court appearance, the judge asked him how to cook a steak. Johnson has been released on bail and was ordered to have no contact with his alleged victim. Inside Edition's Justin Finch has the details.
title: Florida Judge Asks Chef Suspected of Domestic Violence About Cooking Steak

author: Inside Edition
description: A woman who accused TV's former “Bachelor” Clayton Echard of fathering twins who never existed was sentenced to 30 days in jail Friday. Owens appeared in court Friday after pleading guilty to fraudulent schemes, perjury and identity theft. Echard, a reality TV star who is now an Arizona realtor, says his nightmare started after a brief romantic encounter with podcaster Laura Owens in 2023.
title: Laura Owens Sentenced To 1 Month In Jail In Fraud Pregnancy Case

author: Inside Edition
description: Harry Houdini's spectacular death-defying stunts attracted tens of thousands of spectators. This Halloween marks the 100th anniversary of his death, under mysterious circumstances. He promised his wife, Bess, he would make contact from beyond the grave. For years thereafter, she held annual seances every Halloween. Questions still remain about Houdini's death. Fans regularly visit his gravesite in Queens, New York.
title: This Halloween Marks The 100-Year Anniversary Of Houdini's Death

author: Inside Edition
description: The ongoing protests in Paris come at a bad time for the NFL. The New Orleans Saints are playing the Pittsburgh Steelers this Sunday, in the first regular season NFL game held in France. The nationwide protests began in September with student demonstrations and grew into nationwide disruptions over France’s cost-of-living crisis. As Inside Edition's Alison Hall reports, the football game will go on.
title: NFL Game Will Go On Despite Paris Protests

author: Inside Edition
description: A man was arrested after police say he took a sledgehammer to an Iwo Jima statue in Quantico, causing hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage.  The Prince William Police Department said its officers saw the man attacking the statue and knocking off the head of one of the monument's soldiers. The suspect was arrested without incident, authorities said.
title: Virginia Man Accused of Beheading Iwo Jima Statue With Sledgehammer

author: Inside Edition
description: A small business wanted to update its appearance, but after the contractor found an old mural advertising Pepsi underneath the siding, they're going with a retro look. What they uncovered was an old Pepsi advertisement, a real blast from the past. The mural is the talk of the town in Wausau, Wisconsin, especially for a local historian. The new siding planned for this renovation is no longer going up. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Vintage Pepsi Mural Discovered On Building During Renovation

author: Inside Edition
description: As Andres and his wife prepared to board a plane at JFK Airport, they were surrounded by ICE agents. Now she and their dance community are trying to free him. Their GoFundMe campaign is here: https://www.gofundme.com/f/donate-to-help-andres-in-ice-detainment-proceedings
title: Beloved Dance Teacher Detained By ICE #shorts

author: Inside Edition
description: A posterboy for the so-called "looksmaxxing" movement was in court Thursday. Braden Peters, better known to millions of social media followers as Clavicular, appeared at an arraignment in Orleans, Massachusetts. The 20-year-old pleaded not guilty to a rape charge stemming from an alleged sexual assault last year of a then-17-year-old at his family's Cape Cod home. Peters was released on bail and ordered to stay away from the alleged victim and prohibited from making social posts about her. He is due back in court next month.
title: ‘Clavicular’ Pleads Not Guilty To 2025 Cape Cod Rape Charge
